form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Brown introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance

form.official-title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to modify the earned income tax credit to account for the amount by which economic growth has outpaced income growth, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Cost-of-Living Refund Act of 2019.

section.header: Modification of earned income tax credit

paragraph.text: The table in section 32(b)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended—

subparagraph.text: by striking 7.65 in the second column (relating to credit percentage) and inserting 30;
by striking 7.65 in the third column (relating to phaseout percentage) and inserting 15.98;
by striking 34 and inserting 65.28;
by striking 40 and inserting 76.80; and
by striking 45 and inserting 86.40.

paragraph.header: Earned income amount and phaseout amount

subparagraph.text: Subparagraph (A) of section 32(b)(2) of such Code is amended by striking Subject to subparagraph (B), the earned income amount and the phaseout amount and inserting “Subject to subparagraph (B)—

clause.text: The phaseout amount is $18,340.
The earned income amount

subparagraph.text: Section 32(b)(2)(A)(ii) of such Code, as amended by subparagraph (A), is further amended by striking the table and inserting the following:

subsection.text: Subclause (II) of section 32(c)(1)(A)(ii) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking 25 and inserting 21.
Paragraph (1) of section 32(j) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended to read as follows:

paragraph.text: In the case of any taxable year beginning after 2019, each of the dollar amounts in subsections (b)(2) and (i)(1) shall be increased by an amount equal to—

subparagraph.text: such dollar amount, multiplied by
the cost-of-living adjustment determined under section 1(f)(3) for the calendar year in which the taxable year begins, determined by substituting in subparagraph (A)(ii) thereof—

clause.text: in the case of amounts in subsection (b)(2)(A), by substituting calendar year 2018 for calendar year 2016, and
in the case of amounts in subsection (i)(1), by substituting calendar year 1995 for calendar year 2016.

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2018.

section.header: Expansion of earned income tax credit

subsection.header: Inclusion of individuals with qualifying dependents

paragraph.text: Section 32(c)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended—

subparagraph.text: in subparagraph (A), by striking qualifying child each place such term appears and inserting qualifying dependent, and
by striking subparagraphs (B) and (F) and by redesignating subparagraphs (C), (D), and (E) as subparagraphs (B), (C), and (D), respectively.

paragraph.text: Section 32(c) of such Code is amended by redesignating paragraphs (3) and (4) as paragraphs (4) and (5), respectively, and by inserting after paragraph (2) the following:

subparagraph.text: The term qualifying dependent means, with respect to a taxable year—

clause.text: a qualifying child,
a dependent for whom a deduction is allowable under section 151 who—

subclause.text: has attained the age of 65 before the close of the taxable year, or
is an individual described in section 21(b)(1)(B), or

clause.text: an individual described in section 21(b)(1)(C).

subparagraph.text: No credit shall be allowed under this section with respect to a qualifying dependent unless the taxpayer includes the name, age, and TIN of the individual on the return of tax for the taxable year.
The term qualifying dependent shall not include an individual unless such individual has a principal place of abode in the United States for more than one-half of such taxable year.
The tables in paragraphs (1) and (2) of section 32(b) of such Code are each amended—

clause.text: by striking qualifying child each place it appears and inserting qualifying dependent, and
by striking qualifying children each place it appears and inserting qualifying dependents.

subparagraph.text: Section 32(c)(4) of such Code, as redesignated by this Act, is amended by striking subparagraphs (C) and (D).
Section 32(m) of such Code is amended by striking subsections (c)(1)(E) and (c)(3)(D) and inserting subsections (c)(1)(D) and (c)(3)(B).

paragraph.text: Section 32(c)(1)(A) of such Code is amended by striking or at the end of clause (i), by striking the period at the end of clause (ii)(III) and inserting , or, and by inserting after clause (ii)(III) the following new clause:

clause.text: any individual who is a qualifying student.

paragraph.text: Section 32(c)(1) of such Code, as amended by subsection (a), is further amended by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:

clause.text: The term qualifying student means, with respect to a taxable year, an individual who is an eligible student (as defined in section 25A(b)(3)) with respect to an institution of higher education (as defined in section 101 of the Higher Education Act of 1965) who—

item.text: has qualified for a Federal Pell Grant with respect to the academic year beginning in such taxable year, or

whose modified adjusted gross income (as defined in section 24(b)(1)) is less than 250 percent of the poverty line (defined in section 529A(b)(7)(B)) as for the size of the family involved for the taxable year, and

subclause.text: is not a dependent for whom a deduction is allowable under section 151 to another taxpayer for any taxable year beginning in the same calendar year as such taxable year.

clause.text: For purposes of this subparagraph, in determining the poverty line applicable to the taxpayer, the family size with respect to such taxpayer shall be equal to the number of individuals for whom such taxpayer is allowed a deduction under section 151 for the taxable year.

paragraph.text: Section 32(c)(1)(A)(ii) of such Code is amended by inserting (other than a qualifying student) after any other individual.

subsection.header: Minimum credit for students and for individuals with certain qualifying dependents
subsection.text: Section 32(a) of such Code is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph:

paragraph.header: Minimum credit for students and for individuals with certain qualifying dependents

subparagraph.text: In the case of an eligible individual who is a qualifying student or who has a specified dependent for the taxable year, the amount determined under paragraph (1) (before the application of paragraph (2)) and the amount determined under paragraph (2)(A) shall not be less than $1,200.
For purposes of this paragraph, the term specified dependent means any qualifying dependent (other than a qualifying child who has attained the age of 7 before the close of the taxable year).

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after the date of the enactment of this Act.

section.header: Advance payment of earned income credit

subsection.text: Chapter 25 of subtitle C of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by inserting after section 3506 the following new section:

section.header: Advance payment of earned income credit

paragraph.text: An employer making payment of wages to an employee with respect to whom an eligibility certificate is in effect shall, at the time of paying such wages for the payroll period elected by the employee under paragraph (2), make an additional lump sum payment to such employee equal to the earned income advance amount (except as provided in subsection (b)(1)(C)(ii)) of such employee.

paragraph.header: Payments available after 6 months of employment during calendar year
paragraph.text: For purposes of paragraph (1), an employee with respect to whom an eligibility certificate is in effect for the calendar year may elect to receive the earned income advance amount at the same time as wages for any payroll period which begins after the employee has been paid wages by the employer for a period of not less than 6 months during such calendar year.
For purposes of this section, an eligibility certificate is a statement submitted by an employee to the employer which—

subparagraph.text: certifies that the employee is eligible to receive the credit provided by section 32 for the taxable year,
certifies that the employee does not have an eligibility certificate in effect for the calendar year with respect to the payment of wages by another employer, and
certifies that—

clause.text: an eligibility certificate has not been in effect for the spouse of the employee on any date during the calendar year, or
such a certificate is in effect for the spouse of the employee, and the employee is eligible to receive only 1/2 the earned income advance amount otherwise determined with respect to the employee.

paragraph.text: For purposes of this section, an employer shall not—

subparagraph.text: be required to verify any certification made by an employee in the statement described in paragraph (1), or
be held liable for any false claims or statements made by an employee in regards to such statement.
Subject to subparagraph (B), the term earned income advance amount means, with respect to any payroll period, the amount of the credit provided under section 32 as determined—

clause.text: on the basis of the wages of the employee from the employer during such calendar year through such payroll period, and
in accordance with tables issued by the Secretary.

subparagraph.text: For each calendar year, except as provided in subparagraph (C), the earned income advance amount shall not exceed $500.

clause.text: In the case of any taxable year beginning after 2021, the $500 amount in subparagraph (B) shall be increased by an amount equal to—

subclause.text: the cost-of-living adjustment determined under section 1(f)(3) for the calendar year in which the taxable year begins determined by substituting calendar year 2020 for calendar year 2016 in subparagraph (A)(ii) thereof.

clause.text: If any increase determined under paragraph (1) is not a multiple of $10, such increase shall be rounded to the nearest multiple of $10.

paragraph.text: In the case of an employee who is a member of the Armed Forces of the United States, the earned income advance amount shall be determined by taking into account the total wages of such employee, as determined for purposes of section 32.
For purposes of paragraph (1)(A)(ii), the tables issued by the Secretary shall be similar in form to the tables issued under section 3402 and, to the extent feasible, coordinated with such tables.

subsection.header: Payments To be treated as payments of withholding and FICA taxes

paragraph.text: Payments made by an employer under subsection (a) to an employee—

subparagraph.text: shall not be treated as payment of compensation, and
shall be treated as made out of—

clause.text: amounts required to be deducted and withheld for the payroll period under section 3401,
amounts required to be deducted for the payroll period under section 3102, and
amounts of the taxes imposed for the payroll period under section 3111,

subparagraph.continuation-text: as if the employer had paid to the Secretary, on the day on which the wages are paid to the employee, an amount equal to such payments.

paragraph.text: In the case of any employer, if for any payroll period the aggregate amount of earned income advance payments exceeds the sum of the amounts referred to in paragraph (1)(B), the employer shall pay only so much of such earned income advance payment as does not exceed such sum, and shall not make any further advance payments to the employee for the calendar year.

Failure to make any payment of an earned income advance amount as required under this section shall be treated as the failure at such time to deduct and withhold under chapter 24 an amount equal to the earned income advance amount.

An eligibility certificate submitted to an employer at any time during the calendar year shall continue in effect with respect to the employee during such calendar year until revoked by the employee or until another such certificate takes effect under this section.

In the case of an employee who has submitted an eligibility certificate under this section and subsequently becomes ineligible for the credit provided under section 32 for the taxable year, the employee shall, not later than 10 days after becoming ineligible for such credit, submit to the employer a revocation of such certificate.
Eligibility certificates shall be in such form and contain such other information as the Secretary may by regulations prescribe.

subsection.header: Taxpayers making prior fraudulent or reckless claims

paragraph.text: No earned income advance amount shall be paid under this section for any taxable year in the disallowance period.
For purposes of paragraph (1), the disallowance period is—

subparagraph.text: the period of 10 taxable years after the most recent taxable year for which there was a final determination that the taxpayer's claim of an earned income advance amount under this section was due to fraud, and

the period of 2 taxable years after the most recent taxable year for which there was a final determination that the taxpayer's claim of an earned income advance amount under this section was due to reckless or intentional disregard of rules and regulations (but not due to fraud).

subsection.text: The term taxable year means the last taxable year of the employee under subtitle A beginning in the calendar year in which the wages are paid.

The Internal Revenue Service shall take such steps as may be appropriate to ensure that taxpayers who receive a refund of the credit under section 32 are aware of the availability of earned income advance amounts under this section.
Section 32 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by inserting after subsection (f) the following new subsection:

subsection.header: Coordination with advance payments of earned income credit

paragraph.text: If any payment is made to the individual by an employer under section 3507 during any calendar year, then the tax imposed by this chapter for the individual's last taxable year beginning in such calendar year shall be increased by the aggregate amount of such payments.

paragraph.header: Reconciliation of payments advanced and credit allowed
paragraph.text: Any increase in tax under paragraph (1) shall not be treated as tax imposed by this chapter for purposes of determining the amount of any credit (other than the credit allowed by subsection (a)) allowable under this part.

subsection.text: Section 6012(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended—

paragraph.text: in paragraph (7), by striking and at the end,
in paragraph (8), by adding and at the end, and
by inserting after paragraph (8) the following new paragraph:
Every individual who receives payments during the calendar year in which the taxable year begins under section 3507;

subsection.text: Section 6051(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by inserting after paragraph (6) the following new paragraph:

paragraph.text: the total amount paid to the employee under section 3507 (relating to advance payment of earned income credit),

subsection.text: The table of sections for chapter 25 of subtitle C of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by inserting after the item relating to section 3506 the following new item:

toc.toc-entry: Sec. 3507. Advance payment of earned income credit.

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2020.
